answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and propagate trust with a length-bounded random walk, limiting how far endorsements diffuse. A sybil cluster may amplify an echo internally, but its sparse boundary has low conductance, so few walk paths enter from honest nodes. Given explicit trust-distribution assumptions, min-cut bounds constrain its aggregate voting weight by incoming cut flow, not raw node count; labels such as cipher and quartz confer no extra trust.
